splits.text: The parameterization is exact and is based on generalized orthostochastic matrices.
Its computational scaling is O(d³).
A hyperparameter s interpolates between a computationally efficient boundary and the fully expressive Birkhoff polytope.

expansions.text: An orthostochastic matrix is formed by taking the elementwise squared magnitudes of an orthogonal matrix.
The hyperparameter s controls how much of the doubly stochastic matrix space the parameterization can represent.

splits.text: Matrix parameterization geometry increasingly affects the performance and stability of modern machine learning models.
Symmetry and orthogonality are foundational matrix constraints.
Recent manifold-based methods map unconstrained spaces onto constrained geometries such as the Birkhoff polytope.
The Birkhoff polytope enforces doubly stochastic constraints but involves a trade-off between exactness and scalability.

expansions.text: A doubly stochastic matrix has nonnegative entries whose rows and columns each sum to one.
The exactness–scalability trade-off concerns representing every valid constrained matrix without making parameterization or computation impractically large.

splits.text: go-mHC approximates the Birkhoff polytope within error ε(s) using d(d−1)/2 parameters.
mHC-lite provides full coverage of the Birkhoff polytope but requires d! parameters.
KromHC is restricted to B₂ and disallows cycles larger than two.
The parameterization maps a skew-symmetric matrix X to an orthogonal matrix Q with the Cayley transform.
It then maps Q to a doubly stochastic matrix B using block-wise Frobenius norms.
Hyper-Connections are integrated into the residual stream as x_{l+1}=ℋ_l^{res}x_l+Layer F(x_l).
The doubly stochastic constraint is intended to improve training stability and gradient flow.

expansions.text: The Cayley transform converts a suitable skew-symmetric matrix into an orthogonal matrix without requiring explicit orthogonality constraints during optimization.
The Frobenius norm of a matrix block is the square root of the sum of its squared entries.
The comparison separates approximation efficiency, complete coverage, and restricted exact parameterizations as different design points.

splits.text: The parameter count scales as O(d·d!).
This scaling becomes super-exponential in practical dimension d.
At d=8, the method requires 8!=40,320 permutation matrices.
The resulting memory requirement is prohibitive without sampling approximations.

expansions.text: Factorial growth eventually dominates polynomial growth even for moderate matrix dimensions.

splits.text: At s=1, the method lies on the orthostochastic boundary.
As s approaches infinity, the method approaches the dense interior of the Birkhoff polytope.

expansions.text: Increasing s expands the represented region from a constrained boundary toward more general doubly stochastic matrices.

splits.text: The method can be used simultaneously with KromHC.
This combination allows larger Kronecker factors.
The combination mitigates the super-exponential scaling introduced by mHC-lite.

expansions.text: Kronecker factors let a large structured matrix be represented through products of smaller matrices.

splits.text: B_d denotes the closed set of d-dimensional doubly stochastic matrices.
The matrices satisfy M^T J_d=M J_d=J_d.

expansions.text: J_d denotes the all-ones vector or matrix-compatible all-ones object of dimension d, depending on the surrounding notation.
The equalities express preservation of the all-ones direction by both M and its transpose.

splits.text: mHC-lite uses the Birkhoff–von Neumann theorem to define learned connections as convex combinations of permutation matrices.
The construction uses d! permutation matrices.
This approach attempts to eliminate the approximation gap.

expansions.text: A convex combination uses nonnegative weights that sum to one.
The Birkhoff–von Neumann theorem states that every doubly stochastic matrix can be expressed as a convex combination of permutation matrices.

splits.text: KromHC uses tensor products to train residual connections on a smaller set of exactly doubly stochastic matrices.
KromHC sacrifices expressivity and complete coverage of B_d.
Its computational cost is O(d² C).

expansions.text: A tensor product combines smaller factor matrices into a structured larger matrix.
The method exchanges representational coverage for lower computational cost.

splits.text: The orthostochastic transform takes the squared Frobenius norm of matrix blocks.
This operation removes information about reflections.
The resulting representation retains only positive-determinant solutions.
This is sufficient for full coverage.

expansions.text: Squaring block norms makes distinct transformations that differ only by reflection indistinguishable in the projected representation.

splits.text: Xie et al. (2026) use Amax Gain Magnitude to quantify worst-case amplification.
The quantity is applied to the residual hyper-connection product H_{l→L}^{res}=∏_{i=1}^{L−l}H_{L−i}^{res}.

expansions.text: The residual hyper-connection product represents the cumulative linear transformation across residual layers from l to L.
Worst-case amplification measures how strongly perturbations can grow under the cumulative residual transformation.

splits.text: For s=1 and d=3, the learned maps cover the spectral region inside the Karpelevič region of B₃\B₂ up to error ε(s=1).
They also cover real eigenvalues on the interval [−1,1].
The interval [−1,1] is the Karpelevič region associated with B₂.

expansions.text: The spectrum of a matrix is the set of its eigenvalues.
The Karpelevič region characterizes which eigenvalues can occur for matrices in a specified stochastic-matrix class.

splits.text: Expressivity is evaluated using the spectrum of matrices constructed with P_M as a surrogate.
The evaluation measures how many unique matrices can be spanned by their eigenvalues.

expansions.text: A surrogate metric evaluates an indirect property that is used as a proxy for the target property.
The spectral surrogate treats diversity of eigenvalue configurations as evidence of representational coverage.

splits.text: The spectral reach of the Kronecker-parameterized manifold is invariant to the number of products.
Adding more products does not expand the reachable Karpelevič region.
For d>i_k, the reachable region represents a negligible portion of B_d.

expansions.text: Kronecker composition increases structural factorization depth without increasing the relevant spectral degrees of freedom.

splits.text: Model performance improvements generally outweigh their computational cost.
Scaling residual streams eventually reaches a practical computational limit.
go-mHC targets a balance between FLOP cost and expressivity.

expansions.text: Residual-stream scaling increases the amount of information propagated between layers but also increases computation and memory demands.

splits.text: go-mHC has an intermediate FLOP complexity for scaling residual streams.
It avoids the super-exponential cost of mHC-lite.
It avoids the iterative overhead of mHC SK iterations.
The nominal constants are S=20, i_k=2, and s∈{1,2}.
Full complexity estimates are provided in Appendix B.6.

expansions.text: The proposed operating point prioritizes a usable computation–expressivity trade-off rather than minimizing either quantity alone.

splits.text: go-mHC convergence depends on the geometry of the loss landscape induced by manifold M.
Gradient stability is another determinant of convergence.
The method is expected to have learnable gradients.
The method is expected to converge.
The method is expected to be fully connected and able to reach any target matrix.
Proofs are provided in Appendix B.7.

expansions.text: A fully connected parameterization can represent every target matrix in the intended matrix space.
Gradient stability matters because unstable gradients can prevent optimization from reaching regions represented by the manifold.

splits.text: The synthetic experiment generates ground-truth doubly stochastic matrices T_i.
It generates dense residual-stream activations X_j.
It forms noisy targets as Y_{i,j}=T_iX_j+ξ.
The experiment evaluates reconstruction capability.

expansions.text: The noise term ξ makes reconstruction assessment reflect imperfect observations rather than exact matrix multiplication alone.
Successful reconstruction indicates that the parameterization can recover the transformation applied to dense activations under noise.
